items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its moving-average stack, then overlay the option-flow call fraction and put-versus-call premium and the VIX band to judge whether an index holding near its high is being carried by a set of leaders that has narrowed but not collapsed.
items.note: A mild narrow-leadership divergence carries into the pre-market window. The SPY benchmark last printed 769.91, only 1.02% under its 52-week high, in a bull-stacked moving-average regime (50-day distance +2.63%, 200-day +9.34%, 126-day momentum +12.78%), yet just 55.23% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day — a 4.77-point shortfall to the 60% broad-participation threshold. Premium flow is not confirming the strength: it reads balanced-to-defensive, with calls only 46.3% of premium (about $482M of call premium against $558M of puts) across 12 tickers and 717 flagged contracts. VIX 15.41 keeps this in a calm, pressure-not-panic band, while swing structure reads bull-stacked with an active, qualified double-top pattern over 520 bars. A headline index pinned near its high on roughly 55% breadth, with a double top forming overhead and premium flow no longer call-led, is a milder version of the thinning-leadership pattern: participation is broader than a deep divergence but still under the healthy line. What to watch is whether breadth re-broadens back above the 60% threshold or the tape converges down toward the narrower leaders.
items.title: SPY holds about 1.0% under its 52-week high in a bull-stacked regime while daily breadth stalls just below 60% and premium flow no longer leans call-led

items.method: Read the options-structure signed net-gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current spot, size the expected-move band, confirm the dealer scenario and hold from the gamma playbook, then overlay the most-unusual option prints and the intraday session type and VWAP to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearest wall.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price have converged on a pinched gamma corridor this window. Signed net gamma is negative at about -$1.32B, and SPY spot 768.84 sits just below the 769.45 flip, wedged between the 765 put wall and the 770 call wall. The front expected move is plus or minus 4.26 across three priced expiries, so both walls sit near the edges of the modelled band. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so sustained pressure toward a wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The flow tape is balanced overall, but the most unusual prints are downside-hedge-shaped: a same-day QQQ 715 put at $25.6M on 8.4x open interest, a same-day SPY 769 put at $17.0M on 23.4x open interest, and an IWM 302 put at $2.58M. The live auction is a range day under algo-controlled conditions with VWAP 769.77 just above spot after a 0.39% gap-up open. This is a coiled range-break-watch structure with a patient, same-session-fade playbook: while 765 holds and VIX 15.41 stays calm it can stay orderly, but a sustained loss of the 765 put wall in short gamma is what would tip the balance toward downside acceleration rather than an orderly fade.
items.title: SPY spot rests between the 765 put wall and 770 call wall just below the 769.45 negative-gamma flip as the same-day tape lifts hedge puts in QQQ and SPY
